newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech files complaints against MCI, AT&T.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech files complaints against MCI, AT&T.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said Wednesday it filed a complaint with the Federal Communications Commission alleging in the last year AT&T Corp and MCI Communications Corp have switched tens of thousands of customers to their telephone services without permission.

Ameritech said it tracked the practice, known as "slamming", from July 1996 to June 1997 and found 48 percent or 33,940 of the 71,033 complaints it received were against MCI and AT&T. Ameritech asked the FCC to investigate their procedures for switching a customers' long distance or local toll call service.
An MCI spokesman denied the claims and an AT&T spokesman said the company had not seen the filing. Both companies said they have led the industry in opposing slamming.
MCI called the filing "totally misleading", and said Ameritech apparently classifies all disputes over carriers as slamming.
"They're using this as a calculated scare tactic," said Brad Burns, a spokesman for MCI.
Ameritech is facing competition in local toll calling in Illinois, Wisconsin and parts of Michigan.
"We welcome competition into our market, we just don't want slamming to come with it," said Rich Maganini, a spokesman for Ameritech.
